A person s kin are people who are related to the person birth, through family lines and in recent years, kinship roles have undergone a dramatic change.�� In pioneer times, the extended kinship group was usually close, including parents, children, grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins.� In our modern society, people are much more mobile and the kin group isn t as prevalent was before.� Nuclear families, of parents and children are much more common, as these families often live far away from other relatives.�

Think of an important decision that your family has made in the past six months.� A nuclear family usually makes its decision without input from outside sources unless they seek advice from friends or counselors.� In pioneer times, grandparents, aunts and uncles would have some say in the matter.

Although being independent from the kinship group may be seen as beneficial, there are drawbacks too.� If someone was sick or in financial distress, all relatives would have been there to offer support.� Although now you may get help from friends, you may also need to use social programs for help.� Now, grandparents are finding that some grown children are moving back home because of financial stress.� Sometimes grandparents are asked to raise their grandchildren, which moves them back into a parental role.
